truth_evidence: Affected every release before 2.3.0; fixed in 2.3.0. The Authorization header (including one derived from ~/.netrc) was kept on a redirect to another host.
The advisory links no commit, only issue #1885. The fix was found with git log -S Authorization between v2.2.1 and v2.3.0 in requests/sessions.py.

7ba5a534 'Repopulate ~/.netrc auth' (2014-01-29) adds, inside resolve_redirects, the deletion of the Authorization header when the hostname changes and a fresh netrc lookup for the new host. https://github.com/psf/requests/commit/7ba5a534ae9fc24e40b3ae6c480c9075d684727e
326a22e8 'Better layout for checking' and d9f34c68 'Respect trust_env on redirect' complete the same block (no KeyError dance; netrc only when trust_env).
97cf16e9 (part of PR #1951, the CVE-2014-1830 fix) later moves this block unchanged into the new rebuild_auth method; it is a refactor of this fix, not part of it.
Entry points: Session.send calls resolve_redirects for every request with allow_redirects, so every request function and Session method leads to it.
